title: Identity and Equality
purpose: Seed strict identity, equality, equivalence and substitution boundaries so Lantern can recognize sameness without collapsing aliases, similar objects, equal values, versions, claims or distributed nodes into one entity.

concepts.definition: a = b states that a and b denote the same object within the active formal interpretation.
a != b states that a and b denote distinct objects within the active formal interpretation.
Two values are equal under a declared value semantics without implying that their carriers/objects are identical.
A declared relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; equivalent objects need not be identical.
The set of objects mutually equivalent under a declared equivalence relation.
A name/form that refers to an entity; multiple aliases may denote one entity, but similar names do not establish co-reference.
Two references co-refer when evidence establishes that they denote the same entity in context.
For strict identity, a=b permits substitution in extensional predicates when scope/context does not make the expression intensional or time-indexed.
A later version may be historically continuous with an earlier object while differing in state; continuity/version relation is not automatically strict equality across time-indexed states.
Two structures may satisfy a declared equivalence/isomorphism criterion without being the same object.
Two expressions may convey equivalent content under a declared interpretation without being the same string, event, source or claim record.

guards.reason: Distinct objects may carry equal values.
Sharing one or many properties does not establish strict identity.
Equivalence is weaker than strict identity unless R is explicitly identity.
Similarity never establishes identity by itself.
Name similarity does not prove both references denote the same entity.
Independent claims/sources may have identical wording and must retain provenance.
Hive nodes may share experience/knowledge while remaining distinct embodiments/processes.
Continuity does not imply unchanged state.
Substitution inside belief/quotation/intensional contexts may fail when the agent does not know the identity.
Identity does not erase differences between time-indexed claims.

invariants: Strict identity, value equality, similarity and equivalence are distinct relations.
Identity is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
Equivalence relations are reflexive, symmetric and transitive but do not imply strict identity.
Entity resolution requires evidence of coreference; names and labels alone are insufficient.
Independent provenance records remain distinct even when their content is semantically or textually equivalent.
Hive membership/shared memory does not collapse distinct nodes into one record or embodiment.
Substitution by identity is bounded by context: quotation, belief, modality and time may block naive substitution.
Historical/version continuity is represented separately from equality of all states.
Identity inference never grants permissions, ownership or authority.

provenance.authoring_basis: Classical identity/equality and equivalence-relation foundations, adapted for provenance, intensional contexts, versioning and Lantern hive identity.
